reforms.description: Japan introduced an investment tax credit for R&D in 2003, allowing firms to deduct R&D expenditures from corporate income tax liability. This indirect support instrument aims to incentivize private-sector research and development investment.
reforms.growth_orientation_rationale: R&D tax credits reduce the effective cost of private R&D investment, incentivizing firms to increase innovation spending and productivity-enhancing research, thereby supporting long-term GDP growth.
reforms.status_evidence: Text states 'Japan introduced an investment tax credit for R&D in 2003', indicating the reform was in force.
reforms.importance_rationale: A significant but narrower reform introducing a new indirect support instrument for private R&D; not a system-wide structural change.
reforms.source_quote: Following the introduction of an investment tax credit for R&D in 2003, the amount of revenue lost by special deductions in the national corporate income tax increased from 0.4 to 1.7 trillion yen (0.3 per cent of GDP).

reforms.description: Japan established special zones for structural reform in 2002 allowing regulatory experimentation at the local level. Proposals were solicited from local governments, citizens, and enterprises through five rounds of consultation, with accepted proposals implemented either in designated special zones or nation-wide, and an Evaluation Committee assessing outcomes for potential national rollout.
reforms.growth_orientation_rationale: While the special zones framework enables regulatory experimentation that could support innovation, the text does not specify innovation-focused outcomes or R&D-related regulatory changes. The growth effect depends on the nature of experiments conducted, which is not detailed.
reforms.status_evidence: Text states 'Japan established special zones for structural reform', indicating the reform was in force by 2002.
reforms.importance_rationale: A structural, system-wide reform establishing a new governance mechanism for regulatory experimentation across Japan, with potential for nation-wide rollout of successful innovations.
reforms.source_quote: The creation of special zones is based on a mix of local initiative, informal consultations, and central government approval... Thus far, there have been five rounds, each lasting around a month, resulting in more than 2300 reform proposals from nearly 1500 entities.
